source_findings: The pinned OpenAI-Realtime router parses conversation.item.truncate but deliberately treats it as a no-op after cancellation because client-side playback is considered owner of the unheard tail.
At the pinned revision, response cancellation closes the current response and calls Chat.rollback_provisional_generation for cancelled, failed or incomplete responses.

The pinned language-model process makes default-chat commit contingent on the generation not being cancelled and rolls back recorded provisional generation items in its cleanup path when the interrupted generation was not committed.
Pinned upstream tests explicitly assert that a cancelled provisional assistant/tool generation leaves chat.buffer empty while already committed user input survives cancellation.
current_f2_contract_findings: VoiceOutputPacket permits commit_eligible only when playback_state is completed and heard_fraction is exactly 1.0.
advance_output preserves heard_fraction as monotone playback evidence but makes interrupted/cancelled output non-commit-eligible.
barge-in changes queued output to cancelled and started/heard output to interrupted while revoking commit eligibility and fencing outstanding tool ownership.
session close permits a result reference only when at least one fully heard completed output is commit-eligible.

reconciliation.superseded_overstrong_hypothesis: A prior version of this addendum treated loss of an actually heard prefix from server-local next-turn Chat as a product failure unless F2 reconstructed that prefix.
reconciliation.correction: That requirement is not supported by the current F2 commit contract. A partially heard interrupted response is non-commit-eligible as a whole. heard_fraction is retained as playback/diagnostic evidence, not as a rule that the heard semantic prefix must become committed model-context truth.
reconciliation.current_interpretation: Whole-response rollback in the pinned HF server can therefore be compatible with current F2 semantics. It remains a protocol-surface difference from audio_end_ms truncate behavior, but it is not by itself a Frankenstein product negative.

protocol_difference.openai_reference_semantics: conversation.item.truncate is a playback-synchronization operation at a client-supplied audio_end_ms boundary and successful handling is surfaced by conversation.item.truncated.
protocol_difference.pinned_hf_semantics: conversation.item.truncate is accepted as a no-op; cancellation/provisional-generation rollback governs server-local assistant history instead.
protocol_difference.runtime_risk: The material risks are cancelled-response semantics regaining next-turn/tool/effect authority, playback continuing beyond the measured stop boundary, or stale/duplicate cancellation corrupting a newer turn. Dropping the whole interrupted assistant response from raw HF Chat is not presently a failure by itself.

hypotheses.claim: Cancellation rollback should prevent provisional assistant/tool content from the cancelled response from regaining ordinary server-local next-turn authority.

Deleting the whole interrupted assistant response from server-local Chat is compatible with current F2 policy because interrupted output is wholly non-commit-eligible, even when heard_fraction is greater than zero.

F2 must continue to own commit/tool/effect authority independently of speech-server Chat. Explicit partial-prefix context reconstruction becomes required only if a later canonical F2 contract promotes partially heard interrupted semantics into committed conversational context.

falsifier.action: Generate an assistant response with two semantically unique clauses A and B. Allow A to become definitely audible while B remains buffered/unheard. Record the exact F2 heard boundary, issue response.cancel and conversation.item.truncate, inspect server-local Chat and exact next-turn model input, then deliver late tool/audio events and repeat duplicate/stale cancellation/truncate cases.
must_hold: The F2 output packet remains interrupted/cancelled and commit_eligible=false after barge-in even when heard_fraction is greater than zero.
No assistant text/audio/tool/effect semantics from the cancelled non-commit-eligible response regain authoritative next-turn influence.
Playback stops at the measured cancellation/heard boundary and late cancelled-generation audio is discarded.
Late tool results from the cancelled turn cannot reacquire current-turn ownership.
Duplicate, stale or out-of-range cancellation/truncate cannot mutate a newer turn, resurrect cancelled output or increase commit eligibility.
Raw HF Chat may contain neither A nor B after rollback without that alone being classified as failure under the current F2 commit contract.
falsifier.must_not_fail_merely_if: The raw HF server drops the entire interrupted assistant response, including an already-audible prefix, provided F2 retains the measured playback evidence, keeps the response non-commit-eligible and no separate current F2 contract requires partial-prefix semantic persistence.
falsifier.falsifies_if: Any cancelled response semantics regain authoritative next-turn/tool/effect influence, playback exceeds the admitted stop boundary, or stale/duplicate control corrupts a newer causal turn.

execution_routing.note: The older WP715 workflow remains a queued zero-step control-plane subject and must not be converted into HF protocol runtime evidence by association.
